experiment_description: Central concept: bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) generated by high-gain spontaneous parametric down-conversion is used as a quantum-light driver for high-harmonic generation, so the source must be characterized in photon statistics and spectral Schmidt-mode content before using it for attosecond quantum spectroscopy. A commercial femtosecond Yb:YAG fiber laser supplies near-infrared pump pulses at 1030 nm, 2 mJ pulse energy, 140 fs duration, and tunable repetition rate from 1 Hz to 10 kHz. A reduced-diameter portion of the pump is sent through two tandem type-I BBO crystals, each 3 mm thick, separated by approximately 40 cm to favor the lowest-divergence spatial mode. The SPDC output is spectrally filtered by a band-pass filter centered at 2050 nm with 100 nm FWHM to target the degenerate Schmidt mode. The single-pulse spectrum of the filtered quantum light is recorded with an AvaSpec-NIR256-2.5-HSC-EVO near-infrared spectrometer. More than 10000 single-shot spectra I(lambda) are analyzed by constructing the intensity covariance Cov(lambda,lambda') = <I(lambda)I(lambda')> - <I(lambda)><I(lambda')>, normalizing it to C(lambda,lambda') = Cov(lambda,lambda') / integral integral Cov(lambda,lambda') dlambda dlambda', and applying singular-value decomposition to extract orthonormal spectral Schmidt modes u_m(lambda) and mode weights lambda_m. Photon-number statistics are evaluated shot by shot; the time-domain zero-delay second-order correlation is defined here as g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2, where N is the photon number per pulse in the measured filtered BSV mode. The optical path and measurement target the full collected SPDC beam after filtering rather than a selected spatial subregion; the spectral scope covers the near-infrared SPDC band around 1.8-2.3 micrometers, with spectral homogeneity assessed through the Schmidt-mode decomposition of the >10000-shot covariance matrix.

filtered_bsv_spectral_center_nm.description: The measured central wavelength of the spectrally filtered degenerate-mode BSV output.

filtered_bsv_time_domain_g2_tau0.description: The measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the filtered BSV using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2.

filtered_bsv_average_pulse_energy_uJ.description: The measured average pulse energy of the filtered BSV output used for downstream high-harmonic driving.

filtered_bsv_photon_number_per_pulse.description: The estimated photon number per pulse of the filtered BSV output.

filtered_bsv_squeezing_parameter.description: The squeezing parameter inferred for the filtered BSV output.

experiment_description: Central concept: high-harmonic generation in a solid is driven by a spectrally filtered degenerate-mode BSV field to test whether quantum photon-number fluctuations of the infrared driver are transferred to ultraviolet harmonics and whether the harmonic photon statistics can diagnose microscopic intraband-versus-interband emission channels. The quantum-light source is produced by high-gain type-I SPDC in two tandem 3 mm BBO crystals pumped at 1030 nm by 140 fs Yb:YAG pulses, with the SPDC output filtered by a 2050 nm, 100 nm FWHM band-pass filter. The filtered BSV driver is focused by an off-axis parabolic mirror of focal length 25.4 mm into the active region of a 200 micrometer thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal. The driver polarization is aligned along the crystal Gamma-Z axis. The driving intensity is set in the strong-field, nonperturbative solid-state HHG regime and approaches 1.2 TW/cm2 for the main single-mode measurement. Harmonics emitted from the illuminated through-thickness interaction volume are collected by a matching off-axis parabolic mirror and spectrally resolved with a Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer equipped with a PIX-100B high-efficiency detector. The measurement records single-pulse-resolved harmonic spectra, and photon-number distributions are evaluated separately for individual harmonic orders in the 2nd through 10th order range. For each harmonic order, N denotes the photon number in the spectral peak assigned to that harmonic order, and the reported photon bunching metric is g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2. The spectral-geometric scope is the collected emission from the focused spot in the 200 micrometer LN crystal, with harmonic coverage spanning the 2nd-10th orders of the approximately 2060 nm driver; comparison to the lithium niobate field-free bandgap of 3.3 eV provides the physical context for below-gap and above-gap harmonic channels.

highest_detected_harmonic_order_single_m.description: The highest harmonic order detected from x-cut lithium niobate under filtered BSV driving in the measured 2nd-10th harmonic range.

fourth_harmonic_g2_tau0.description: The measured zero-delay photon-number correlation for the fourth harmonic using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2.

fifth_harmonic_g2_tau0.description: The measured zero-delay photon-number correlation for the fifth harmonic using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2.

eighth_harmonic_g2_tau0.description: The measured zero-delay photon-number correlation for the eighth harmonic using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2.

tenth_harmonic_g2_tau0.description: The measured zero-delay photon-number correlation for the tenth harmonic using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2.

single_mode_bsv_harmonic_g2_order_depend.description: The measured qualitative dependence of harmonic photon bunching on harmonic order across the 2nd-10th harmonics.

single_mode_bsv_harmonic_g2_peak_order.description: The harmonic order at which the measured g2_tau0 is largest within the 2nd-10th harmonic range.

experiment_description: Central concept: the proposed attosecond quantum-spectroscopy observable is the harmonic-order dependence of g2_tau0, so the experiment tests whether the same increase-then-decrease photon-bunching pattern persists when the filtered BSV driving intensity is changed. The BSV source is produced by the same 1030 nm, 140 fs Yb:YAG-pumped tandem type-I BBO SPDC geometry with two 3 mm BBO crystals separated by approximately 40 cm and with a 2050 nm, 100 nm FWHM band-pass filter selecting the degenerate spectral mode. The filtered BSV is focused by an f = 25.4 mm off-axis parabolic mirror into a 200 micrometer thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal, with polarization along the Gamma-Z axis. Harmonic emission from the focused interaction region is collected by a second off-axis parabolic mirror and recorded shot by shot with a Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer and PIX-100B detector. The independent variable is harmonic order over the measured 2nd-10th range, and the fixed comparison driving intensities are 0.57 TW/cm2 and 0.98 TW/cm2. For each harmonic order and intensity, the photon-number statistic is computed from the single-shot distribution using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2, where N is the photon number in the corresponding harmonic spectral peak. The spatial scope is the collected output from the same focused spot geometry through the 200 micrometer LN crystal for both intensities, enabling comparison of order-dependent photon statistics under otherwise matched material orientation and detection conditions.

g2_order_dependence_at_0p57_and_0p98_TW_.description: The measured qualitative harmonic-order dependence of g2_tau0 across the tested pair of driving intensities.

experiment_description: Central concept: without spectral filtering, the same high-gain SPDC source is intended to supply a low-dimensional multimode BSV containing non-degenerate Schmidt modes, i.e. bright entangled photon-pair components, whose wavelength-resolved correlations can be mapped through high-harmonic generation. The source uses near-infrared 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs pulses from the Yb:YAG laser at a tunable 1 Hz-10 kHz repetition rate, with a reduced-diameter beam sent into two 3 mm thick type-I BBO crystals in tandem and separated by approximately 40 cm to select the first spatial mode. No band-pass filter is placed after SPDC, so the collected near-infrared output contains the accessible lower-order spectral Schmidt modes of the generated BSV. The full collected SPDC beam is characterized with an AvaSpec-NIR256-2.5-HSC-EVO near-infrared spectrometer over the approximately 1800-2300 nm spectral interval. More than 10000 single-shot spectra are used for Schmidt-mode decomposition through the covariance matrix Cov(lambda,lambda'), its normalized form C(lambda,lambda'), and singular-value decomposition of the square-root matrix to obtain spectral modes and relative weights. Photon-number statistics are measured shot by shot over the collected multimode field, with g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2. Wavelength-resolved intensity correlations are computed as g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>), where N(lambda) is the photon number in a spectral bin centered at wavelength lambda. The normalized correlation parameter is Gamma(lambda,lambda') = [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda)g2(lambda')], with g2(lambda) defined as g2(lambda,lambda). The correlation maps target diagonal autocorrelation features and off-diagonal inter-wavelength co-fluctuations across the measured near-infrared BSV spectral band.

unfiltered_multimode_bsv_average_pulse_e.description: The measured average single-pulse energy reached by the unfiltered multimode BSV source under the stated operating constraints.

unfiltered_multimode_bsv_time_domain_g2_.description: The measured zero-delay second-order photon-number correlation of the unfiltered multimode BSV field using g2_tau0 = <N^2>/<N>^2.

unfiltered_bsv_off_diagonal_spectral_cor.description: Whether the wavelength-resolved g2(lambda,lambda') and Gamma(lambda,lambda') maps contain off-diagonal inter-wavelength correlation features beyond the diagonal autocorrelation ridge.

experiment_description: Central concept: the non-degenerate bright entangled photon-pair components in the unfiltered BSV driver are used to test whether quantum-induced spectral correlations survive the strongly nonlinear up-conversion process into harmonic light. The unfiltered BSV driver is generated by high-gain type-I SPDC in two tandem 3 mm BBO crystals pumped by 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs Yb:YAG pulses, with approximately 40 cm crystal spacing and no spectral band-pass filter after SPDC. The resulting multimode quantum light is focused by an f = 25.4 mm off-axis parabolic mirror into a 200 micrometer thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal, with the driver polarization aligned along the Gamma-Z axis. The emitted harmonics from the focused through-thickness interaction region are collected by a matching off-axis parabolic mirror, dispersed by the Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer, and recorded shot by shot with a PIX-100B detector. The third-order harmonic is analyzed over the approximately 600-750 nm wavelength interval. Single-shot spectra are used both to compare total averaged third-harmonic spectra with subsets of pulses selected by their spectral structure and to compute wavelength-resolved correlations. The measured correlation functions are g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>) and Gamma(lambda,lambda') = [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda)g2(lambda')], where g2(lambda)=g2(lambda,lambda) and N(lambda) is the photon number in a third-harmonic wavelength bin. The analysis targets diagonal autocorrelation and off-diagonal lobes aligned with harmonic wavelengths associated with the non-degenerate Schmidt-mode sidebands, without using absolute intensity as the correlation metric.

third_harmonic_wavelength_resolved_g2_la.description: The measured peak pattern in the wavelength-resolved marginal second-order correlation g2(lambda) of the third harmonic.

third_harmonic_off_diagonal_g2_correlati.description: Whether the measured third-harmonic g2(lambda,lambda') map contains off-diagonal wavelength-correlation lobes beyond the diagonal autocorrelation ridge.

third_harmonic_off_diagonal_gamma_correl.description: Whether the measured third-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map contains off-diagonal wavelength-correlation lobes beyond the diagonal autocorrelation ridge.

bep_contribution_detected_in_third_harmo.description: Whether the third-harmonic spectral-correlation measurements detect a contribution associated with the non-degenerate bright entangled photon-pair components of the driver.

experiment_description: Central concept: the multimode BSV/BEP-driven HHG experiment is extended across harmonic orders to determine the harmonic-order range over which non-degenerate-pair-induced wavelength correlations remain spectrally resolvable after up-conversion. The unfiltered BSV source is generated from 1030 nm, 2 mJ, 140 fs Yb:YAG pump pulses in two 3 mm type-I BBO crystals separated by approximately 40 cm, with no spectral filter after SPDC. The multimode BSV is focused with an f = 25.4 mm off-axis parabolic mirror into a 200 micrometer thick free-standing x-cut lithium niobate crystal, with polarization along the Gamma-Z axis. Harmonic emission from the focused interaction volume is collected by a matching off-axis parabolic mirror and recorded as single-shot spectra with the Princeton Instruments HRS-500 spectrometer and PIX-100B detector. The second-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map is evaluated over approximately 950-1100 nm, and the fourth-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map is evaluated over approximately 450-550 nm. Gamma(lambda,lambda') is defined as [g2(lambda,lambda')]^2/[g2(lambda)g2(lambda')], with g2(lambda,lambda') = <N(lambda)N(lambda')>/(<N(lambda)><N(lambda')>) and g2(lambda)=g2(lambda,lambda). The spatial and spectral scope is the collected emission from the same LN focus, with maps inspected for off-diagonal inter-wavelength correlation structures as the indicator of BEP-related harmonic contributions.

second_harmonic_off_diagonal_gamma_corre.description: Whether the measured second-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map contains off-diagonal inter-wavelength correlation features.

fourth_harmonic_off_diagonal_gamma_corre.description: Whether the measured fourth-harmonic Gamma(lambda,lambda') map contains off-diagonal inter-wavelength correlation features.

highest_harmonic_order_with_detected_bep.description: The highest harmonic order for which the experiments detect a BEP-related contribution to the harmonic emission under the stated multimode BSV driving conditions.
